picks.style: ancient greek hymn, lyre and aulos, clear male voice with soft chorus, modal, reverent, slow
picks.why: The wreath from the unmown meadow — the play's most quoted lyric and a complete image on its own.

picks.style: ancient chorus, kithara, frame drum, layered female voices, keening, dark, building
picks.why: The white-winged ship carrying the bride to her doom, closing on the cry that the queen has hanged herself.

picks.style: ancient processional lament, double aulos, unison girls' choir, solemn, slow, ritual
picks.why: Artemis's promise that unwed girls will cut their hair for him forever — a built-in ritual refrain.

picks.style: roman comic patter, tibia pipes, hand drum and clappers, brash male voice, brisk, swaggering
picks.why: The prologue's direct address to the audience — hungry or full, sit down and listen; pure stage energy.

picks.style: comic insult aria, shrill tibia and cymbals, ranting male voice, fast, escalating, theatrical
picks.why: The soldier's torrent of abuse — shoe-latchet, skinned pilchard, pot of stinking sea-salt — a list that sings itself.

picks.style: rustic satyr rant, aulos, goatskin drum, gruff bellowing male voice, driving, earthy
picks.why: Silenus lashing his cowardly sons: nothing but body and tongue and voice, trusting words and fleeing deeds.

picks.style: playful pastoral duet, brightly plucked lyre, nymph soprano against rough male chorus, curious, moderate
picks.why: The riddle of the lyre solved — a voice made from a dead animal, and the song that flits like a bee over flowers.

picks.style: hushed storytelling chant, low lyre drone, warm female voice, secretive, unhurried
picks.why: Cyllene's secret: the hidden child in the cave who grew in six days to the height of a young man.

picks.style: georgian glee, harpsichord and traverso flute, clear soprano, light, graceful, lilting
picks.why: Goldfinch, lark and nightingale outsung by a woman's voice — a song explicitly about singing.

picks.style: english cathedral anthem, chamber organ, choir with treble line, majestic, broad, resonant
picks.why: Arise, O Lord — night has no shades for thee; a full-throated sublime hymn with natural refrain shape.

picks.style: baroque ode, strings and continuo, agile tenor, buoyant, rising, ornamented
picks.why: Fancy diving to the coral floor for jasper, sapphire and ruby — concrete, glittering, and self-contained.

picks.style: greek comic chorus, aulos and lyre, rowdy male voices, dance rhythm, merry, rustic
picks.why: Freed from helmet and cheese and onions — the drinking-by-the-fire song, the warmest thing in the play.

picks.style: pastoral greek song, syrinx pipes and lyre, warm male voice, sunlit, ambling, contented
picks.why: The cricket, the ripening Lemnian vines, the swelling fig, and the cry Dear seasons!

picks.style: wedding processional, aulos and tambourine, call-and-response chorus, torchlit, celebratory, quickening
picks.why: The Hymen, Hymenaeus refrain with the prayer for barley, wine, figs and children — a ready-made chorus.

picks.style: mock-tragic declamation, solo lyre, portentous male voice, grandiose then deflating, moderate
picks.why: Gods speaking in borrowed tragic verse about Zeus's sulk — parody that still scans as high style.

picks.style: oracular chant, reedy aulos, sonorous male voice, mock-solemn hexameters, steady, ceremonial
picks.why: Apollo's absurd prophecy — victory lies with the mules — delivered in perfect oracular cadence.

picks.style: aesopic proverb song, plucked lyre, wry male voice, light, unhurried, conversational
picks.why: The fox's many tricks against the hedgehog's one, and the octopus taking the colour of its rock.

picks.style: roman verse epistle, solo lyre, grave male voice, spare, measured, stern
picks.why: The only verse in the batch's letters — a terse exhortation to keep sober and hold what you held as consul.
